program.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Transform the black DVD into a white DVD.
requirements.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD

outcomes.description: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
outcomes.target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
outcomes.reference: The black DVD in the input image.

nodes.question: Was the specific DVD shown in the source image transformed from black to white?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source DVD is identifiable across the images and that same object is visibly white in the edited image. Fail if it remains black or is absent without being transformed. Unknown if the source DVD's correspondence to an edited object cannot be established.
nodes.binding: Track the small rectangular DVD case near the center of the source image into the edited image using its location and surrounding scene. Do not treat a white disc elsewhere, including one over the separate dark animal, as evidence that the source DVD was transformed.

nodes.question: Does the object corresponding to the source DVD remain identifiable as that DVD in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the edited object can be matched to the source DVD and remains identifiable as a DVD. Fail if the source DVD is absent or replaced by an unrelated object. Unknown if correspondence or DVD identity cannot be established.
nodes.binding: Compare the small rectangular DVD case near the center of the source image with candidate objects in the edited image, considering location and surrounding scene. Do not infer identity from a nearby white disc's shape alone; leave correspondence unresolved when the visual evidence is insufficient.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“(...) that DVD”) and the criterion asks whether the source remains identifiable, which does not directly assess the requested transformation from black DVD to white DVD. Repair the binding to anchor the source object by its visible location and distinctive appearance, then compare its corresponding edited object using scene position/context and object features—not shape alone. Evaluate whether the requested color change has progressed, allowing partial progress if the corresponding DVD is visibly transformed but not fully compliant; do not treat unrelated white objects as progress. In these images, the source DVD is the small rectangular case near center, while the edited image shows two white discs and no clearly matched case. The trace’s uncertainty is valid under the current correspondence rule, but it leaves the aggregate unresolved despite the reference “no”; clarify how to distinguish absence/replacement from insufficient evidence without forcing a label. Confidence 0.94 does not resolve that ambiguity. There are no transport, schema, or dependency failures to address.
d1: Repair the truncated binding and align the decision criterion with the requested black-to-white transformation. Anchor the source DVD by its center location and visible rectangular case/cover, then assess correspondence in the edited image using position, surrounding scene, and object features—not shape or color alone. Distinguish a clearly absent or replaced source object from genuinely indeterminate correspondence: absence without visible transformation is not evidence of progress, but do not force “no” when the image cannot establish what happened. The edited image shows a white disc near the source DVD’s area and another over the animal; neither is clearly the same rectangular case, so unrelated white objects must not count as progress. Preserve partial only for visible progress on the matched DVD, and unresolved when correspondence remains genuinely uncertain. Low confidence or repeated variation should prompt investigation, not change the visual standard. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

observations.evidence: The source DVD is the small rectangular case near the center, but that case is not clearly identifiable in the edited image. The edited image shows two white discs, including one over the dark animal; the binding explicitly excludes treating that disc as evidence of the DVD's transformation. The other white disc is not clearly the same object as the source case.

The source DVD is the small rectangular case near the center. In the edited image, that case is no longer visible; two white discs appear, but their shapes alone do not establish which, if either, corresponds to the source DVD. The surrounding scene is similar, but correspondence and DVD identity cannot be established from the visual evidence.

transactions.reason: Both existing checks leave the requirement unresolved because they require confident object correspondence. Replace them with one direct required-condition check that distinguishes visible transformation from absence or genuinely indeterminate correspondence, while excluding unrelated white discs as progress.

decisions.question: Has the source black DVD visibly been transformed into a white DVD in the edited image?
decisions.criteria: Pass only if the source DVD is visibly transformed and is white in the edited image. Fail if the source DVD is clearly unchanged, absent without visible transformation, or replaced by unrelated objects; a white object alone is not progress. Unknown only if the images do not provide enough evidence to determine whether the source DVD was transformed. If the corresponding DVD is visibly transformed but remains partly black, count that as visible progress and fail this complete-condition check.
decisions.binding: Anchor the source object as the small rectangular DVD case near the center of the source image. Compare the edited image using its position, surrounding scene, and object features, not shape or color alone. Do not count either white disc—including the disc over the dark animal—as the source DVD unless the visual evidence establishes that it is the same object. If the source case is clearly gone and no corresponding transformed DVD is visible, treat the requested transformation as not satisfied; reserve unknown for genuine evidential ambiguity.
